title: Boats and Streams
tagline: Year 2 — Downstream, upstream, still-water speed and stream speed

introduction.overview: When a boat moves in a river, the water current helps or opposes it. Moving with the current (downstream) the effective speed is the boat's speed in still water plus the speed of the stream. Moving against the current (upstream) it is the boat's speed minus the stream speed. The whole chapter follows from these two sentences and the basic speed-time-distance relation.
introduction.placementRelevance: Boats and streams questions are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds. They look different from trains but are the same relative-speed idea applied to water.
introduction.realWorldContext: Ferry schedules, river cruises and swimming across a current all depend on speeds with and against the stream.

learningObjectives: Find the boat's speed and the stream's speed from the two
Solve problems involving ratios of speeds and times
Compute average speed for a round trip in a stream

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: D = S × T. Round trip with the same one-way distance: total time = D/downstream + D/upstream.

coreDefinitions: Speed in still water (b): speed of the boat without any current.
Speed of the stream (s): speed of the water current.
Downstream speed = b + s. Upstream speed = b − s.
Boat speed b = (downstream + upstream)/2. Stream speed s = (downstream − upstream)/2.
Average speed for a round trip = 2uv/(u + v) with u and v the downstream and upstream speeds.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The stream is like a moving walkway. With it, you get a free boost; against it, you lose speed. The boat's own speed is the midpoint between its downstream and upstream speeds, and the stream is half the gap between them.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Always find the two effective speeds first. From them the boat speed and stream speed follow. Then each part of the journey is a simple distance ÷ speed.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Effective speeds
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Downstream u = b + s;  Upstream v = b − s

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Boat and stream speeds
importantRulesAndFormulas.whenToUse: When u and v are known.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Ratio form
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: If u : v = p : q then b = (p + q)/(p − q) × s ÷ ... or b : s = (p + q) : (p − q)

mainNarrative: Define b and s. Downstream is b + s and upstream is b − s. If a boat goes 12 km/h downstream and 8 km/h upstream, then b = 10 km/h and s = 2 km/h.
For time and distance, use the right speed for each leg. A boat of speed 8 km/h in a stream of 2 km/h covers 30 km upstream in 30 ÷ 6 = 5 hours.
For a round trip with the same one-way distance D, total time = D/(b + s) + D/(b − s). With b = 15 and s = 5 and D = 40: 40/20 + 40/10 = 6 hours.
To find the stream speed from time data, form an equation in s. With b = 12 and 36 km each way in 8 hours: 36/(12 + s) + 36/(12 − s) = 8, so 36 × 24/(144 − s²) = 8, giving s² = 36 and s = 6.
For ratio problems: if the downstream and upstream speeds are in the ratio 3 : 2, write them as 3x and 2x. Then b = 2.5x and s = 0.5x. If b = 10, then x = 4 and s = 2.

deepDiveAspects.title: Why the average round trip speed is lower than b
deepDiveAspects.content: You spend more time going against the stream (the slow leg), so the average speed is the harmonic mean of the two speeds, which is less than b.

deepDiveAspects.title: Stream speed cannot exceed boat speed
deepDiveAspects.content: If s ≥ b, the boat cannot go upstream. In a problem, b − s must be positive.

solvedExamples.title: Boat and stream from two speeds
solvedExamples.question: A boat goes 15 km/h downstream and 9 km/h upstream. Find the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the stream.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Downstream adds the stream and upstream subtracts it.

solvedExamples.title: Round trip time
solvedExamples.question: A boat's speed in still water is 15 km/h and the stream flows at 5 km/h. How long does it take to go 40 km downstream and return?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The return leg is twice as slow.

solvedExamples.title: Find the stream speed from total time
solvedExamples.question: A boat's speed in still water is 12 km/h. It goes 36 km downstream and returns in a total of 8 hours. Find the speed of the stream.

shortcutMethods.title: Mid-point and half-gap

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Solve two equations for b and s.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Boat speed is the average of downstream and upstream; stream speed is half the difference.

rulesForApplication: u = b + s; v = b − s.

commonMistakes.mistake: Averaging b for round trip speed

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Downstream speed must exceed upstream; the boat speed lies between them.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Always compute u and v first.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Ratio questions convert quickly into b : s ratios.

A man rows to a place 48 km away and back in 14 hours. He rows 4 km downstream in the same time as 3 km upstream. The speed of the stream is
advanced.explanation: Downstream : upstream = 4 : 3 = 4k : 3k. 48/4k + 48/3k = 28/k = 14, so k = 2. Speeds 8 and 6, stream = 1 km/h.
